name: EU Russia Sanctions — Council Regulation (EU) 269/2014 + 833/2014
reference: Council Reg (EU) 269/2014 + Council Reg (EU) 833/2014 + CFSP Decision 2014/145 + 2014/512
supervisor: EU Member State competent authorities + Commission

articles.title: Asset freeze on designated persons (Reg 269/2014 Art. 2)
articles.requirement: All funds + economic resources belonging to, owned, held or controlled by natural / legal persons + entities + bodies listed in Annex I are frozen. No funds or economic resources made available, directly or indirectly, to or for their benefit. Annex I substantially expanded since February 2022 (>2,200 entries by 2025).

articles.title: Reporting obligation (Reg 269/2014 Art. 9)
articles.requirement: Natural / legal persons + entities + bodies supply, immediately, to the competent authority of the Member State where they are resident or located, any information they hold about frozen funds + economic resources, accounts + amounts frozen. Cooperate with the competent authority on verification.

articles.title: Capital markets restrictions (Reg 833/2014 Art. 1-5)
articles.requirement: Prohibition on dealing in transferable securities + money-market instruments of certain Russian state-owned credit institutions + designated entities with maturity exceeding stated thresholds (initially 30 days then progressively tightened). Loan provisioning + correspondent-account restrictions for designated banks. Foreign-currency-denominated transferable securities issued by Russia + designated entities prohibited.

articles.title: Dual-use + advanced-technology export restrictions
articles.requirement: Export to Russia of dual-use items + advanced-technology items (semiconductors, certain electronics, aerospace, navigation, sensors, materials) prohibited or subject to licensing. List in Annex VII. Re-export controls for transit jurisdictions. Substantially expanded across the 14+ sanctions packages adopted since February 2022.

articles.title: Oil + petroleum products + price cap (Reg 833/2014 Art. 3m-3n)
articles.requirement: Import of Russian crude oil + petroleum products into EU prohibited (with limited transitional exceptions). Maritime services (insurance + financing + brokering + flagging + classification) for transport of Russian crude / products to third countries prohibited unless the oil is purchased at or below the G7 + EU + UK price cap ($60/barrel initial; lowered to $47.60/barrel in late 2025). Attestation regime + record-keeping for compliant trades.

articles.title: Prohibited services (Reg 833/2014 Art. 5n)
articles.requirement: Provision (directly or indirectly) of specified services to the Russian Government, persons established in Russia, or for their benefit prohibited: legal advisory services, accounting, auditing, bookkeeping, tax consulting, business + management consulting, public-relations services, architectural + engineering, IT consulting + cloud services, market research, advertising. Limited carve-outs for humanitarian + government-mandated services.

articles.title: Transaction prohibition with designated state-owned entities (Art. 5aa)
articles.requirement: Prohibition on directly or indirectly engaging in any transactions with specified state-owned + state-controlled legal persons + entities + bodies established in Russia (extensive list in Annex XIX). Limited general exceptions for humanitarian + medical + food + judicial proceedings.

articles.title: EU ownership + control attribution
articles.requirement: EU rule: an entity is considered owned by a designated person where >50% of property rights are held by designated persons (aggregated). Control is assessed through criteria including: majority of voting rights; right to appoint / remove a majority of board; dominant influence (de facto control). Commission FAQ + 2024 Notice provides operational guidance — narrower 'control' test than OFSI but with similar substantive effect.

articles.title: Enforcement (Member State responsibility — Art. 215 TFEU)
articles.requirement: EU sanctions are directly applicable but enforcement is via national competent authorities. Penalties set by Member State law (must be effective, proportionate + dissuasive — Directive (EU) 2024/1226 establishing minimum criminal penalties for breaches of EU sanctions adopted 2024, in force from May 2025). Significant national divergence in enforcement intensity — Germany / Netherlands / France most active prosecutors.

articles.title: Sanctions criminalisation Directive (EU) 2024/1226
articles.requirement: EU Directive establishing minimum criminal penalties for breaches of EU sanctions, including circumvention. Member States required to transpose by May 2025. Harmonises sanctions-evasion as a serious criminal offence across the EU; mandates corporate criminal liability + minimum maximum penalty thresholds. Closes the prior 'forum-shopping' gap where some Member States had minimal criminal sanctions enforcement.
